rows.label: How long we would fund program if above bar after the trial (years) (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Assumption. We've typically assumed this in CEAs, but we haven't explored this in depth at all.

rows.label: Probability that we conclude program is above/below bar after the trial (assuming no failure) (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Key parameter. For RCTs, this is probability we update toward believing the program is above our bar. For pilots, this is the probability that we believe the program is above our bar following the pilots.

rows.label: Probability the trial/study fails (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Assumption. This should take into account the probability that trial fails for some reason e.g. pandemic, political instability, half the treatment group getting lost of follow-up etc.

rows.label: Probability that we conclude program is above/below bar after the trial (8x bar for future opportunities)
Best guess on CE of this reallocated funding (x cash) (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Key parameter. This is going to depend on best guesses on CE after the pilot/study. If value comes from learning this is above (below) our bar, then this will be > (<) cost-effectiveness of counterfactual opportunity.

rows.label: Cost-effectiveness of counterfactual opportunity (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Assumption. This is based on forecasted funds raised.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar, GiveDirectly (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Top charities cost-effectiveness analysis

rows.label: Change in funding to program per year if we update (millions) (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Key parameter. For RCTs, this is the change in funding as a result of learning this is above the bar (in which case we move more to the program) or below the bar (in which case we move less to the program), conditional on updating toward believing this is above/below our bar. For pilots, this is the amount of funding that is opened up by optionality.

Cost-effectiveness from the program itself during pilot/trial period (x cash) (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Key parameter.

rows.label: Grant cost going toward direct benefit (millions) (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Key parameter. This is just the cost of implementing the program. This is used to determine direct benefit of the program (i.e., cost-effectiveness of delivering the program, excluding any information or option value).

rows.label: Total units of value created by direct benefits (8x bar for future opportunities)
Total units of value (8x bar for future opportunities)
Total grant cost (millions) (8x bar for future opportunities)
rows.explainer: Key parameter. This is the cost of initial pilot grant or trial, including costs of piloting/trial and costs of implementing the program alongside. For RCTs, this includes data collection, researcher team, etc., and costs of program implementation. For pilot grants, this is likely just implementation, though may also include some additional non-program components (e.g., data collection, etc.).

rows.label: Weighted cost-effectiveness from value of information and program itself (x cash)
Risk that we learn this is above/below our bar and are wrong
rows.explainer: Key parameter. This captures the possibility that we: i) draw a noisy/biased treatment effect from the trial; ii) update our funding decisions according to the trial; iii) make the wrong ex post decision as a result.

rows.label: Risk that pilot/study is funded without us in a few years
rows.explainer: Assumption. This could vary based on likelihood of funging for specific pilot/trial. We shouldn't be assuming trial would never be funded

rows.label: Benefit from influencing other funders/value to broader research community
rows.explainer: Assumption. This parameter captures the idea that the trial we fund could update the funding decisions of other grantmakers/policymakers as well as our own.

rows.label: Downside adjustment
Cost-effectiveness (x cash)
Units of value per dollar given to GiveDirectly
rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.
